newsitem.title: UK: EURO-BOURSES SCALE PEAKS, DOLLAR RALLIES.
newsitem.headline: EURO-BOURSES SCALE PEAKS, DOLLAR RALLIES.

text.p: European share markets burst higher on Wednesday, with London, Frankfurt and Amsterdam scaling new peaks, while the dollar rallied to levels not seen against the yen in more than 2-1/2 years.
The dollar's strength and Wall Street's overnight record close gave European financial markets a decisive shove at the start of business.
London shares brushed past 4,000 points on the blue chip FTSE 100 index for the first time, Frankfurt hit successive highs and takeover fever pushed Amsterdam to a record.
Europe's other major equity market, Paris, traded strongly higher through the morning, Hong Kong had its best finish this year and the Australian stock market ended at a five-month high.
By the European mid-session, the dollar was cruising just below its highs as talk of increased outflows from Japan sent the yen running for cover.
The dollar hit 111.92 yen in early trade, its best level since January 1994. The yen also plunged to a four-year low against the Australian dollar and its worst rate against sterling in 3-1/2 years.
"Dollar/yen could go up to 112 in the near future, simply because of the flows that seem to be coming out of Japan at the moment," said Chris Turner, currency strategist at BZW.
By 1100 GMT the dollar was quoted around 111.78 yen and 1.5250 marks versus Tuesday's late European levels of 111.40 and 1.5261.
Overnight comments from U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan that there were no threats to inflation down the track added to the upbeat mood in Europe.
London's blue chip FTSE 100 index shot through 4,000 points at the opening, then powered to a high of 4,014.4 in early trade, topping its previous best of 3,994.1 set on September 20.
Buying pressure quickly slackened off, however, to leave the market tracking sideways by late morning at 4,006.

London's share traders said an influx of cash at the start of the new quarter, combined with moderate growth and benign inflationary pressures in Britain and the United States provided the backdrop for the stock market's heady rise in recent days.

"In the very short term, it does appear there's quite a lot of cash sitting on the sidelines waiting to come in and that's going to happen sooner rather than later," said Panmure Gordon strategist Ian Williams.

"On a week to two week view there's probably more upside to come... over the fourth quarter as a whole we're still a little bit nervous... but the underlying liquidity driver is going to be the factor in the near future."
Dutch shares hit their own record after news that telecoms group Dutch PTT (KPN) is bidding 2.7 billion guilders ($1.6 billion) for Australia's TNT transport group.
The firmer dollar and Wall Street's gains were cited by German traders as the main factors behind the rise of the 30-share DAX index to a record 2,675.02.
The market also got some support from debt markets although some traders were worried about the prospect of profit-taking before Thursday's national holiday.
French shares started well bid on the back of Wall Street and a firm bond market, with the CAC-40 rising nearly one percent over the morning.
"The market is feeling bullish," said one trader. "New York, London are at historic highs, the franc's doing well, the dollar's looking good."
But another called the market toppy and said the release on Friday of U.S. jobs figures argued in favour of caution.
CURRENCIES AT 1100 GMT
The dollar traded around 111.78 yen and 1.5250 marks versus Tuesday's late European levels of 111.40 and 1.5261.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1100 GMT
London - The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading shares was up 14.2 points at 4,006.4.
Frankfurt - The 30-share DAX index of German shares was up 18.86 at 2,674.59.
Paris - The CAC-40 share index was up 19.38 at 2,142.59.
